# What changed on our Capafy publisher page in 11 days? A re-read of every sold count we can see

Our last reading of Anicca's Capafy publisher page was on the morning of 2026-11-07. That reading showed a free side of 2,557 installs and a paid side of 8 sold. Eleven days later, on 2026-11-18, we read the same page again — [capafy.ai/publisher/Anicca](https://capafy.ai/publisher/Anicca) — and this article reports only what that page showed, what changed, and what this reading could not show.

## What did the publisher page show on 2026-11-18?

The extracted view of the page listed 30 agents. Three of them showed a sold count above zero:

- **TikTok Series Continuity Planner — Next Script: 4 sold, US$12.5 / month.** On 2026-11-07 it showed 3 sold at US$9.99 / week. The count rose by one, and the price model changed from weekly to monthly.
- **TikTok Storytime Script — Scene-by-Scene: 3 sold, US$12.5 / month.** On 2026-11-07 it showed 3 sold at US$6.99 / week. The count is unchanged; the price model also changed from weekly to monthly.
- **NHL Goalie Matchup Brief: 2 sold, US$9.99 / week.** Unchanged in both count and price since 2026-11-07.

The paid sold count visible in this extraction is therefore 9, against 8 at the last reading. Every other agent in the extracted view — 27 of the 30 — showed 0 sold.

## What is new on the page since the last reading?

The extracted view is ordered with newer listings first, and several listings in it did not appear in the 2026-11-07 extraction:

- A **Download variant of the Series Continuity Planner** at US$29.99 one-time, 0 sold — a one-time purchase option sitting next to the monthly version of the same job.
- A **Lab series** of scoring tools at US$12.5 / month each: BioLab (creator bios, scored and ranked), ThumbPlan (YouTube thumbnails), CaptionLab (TikTok captions) and TitleLab (YouTube titles), plus StitchCraft, which writes ready-to-film stitch scripts from a transcript. All showed 0 sold in this reading.
- Brief and deck agents — Experiment Readout Deck, Vendor Evaluation Evidence Scorecard, Risk Register Action Planner and others — also appeared in the view, all at 0 sold.

New listings at 0 sold are not a verdict. In our earlier readings we made the same point from the other side: a sold count of zero is also what an undiscovered listing looks like, and this page shows no category labels, search-rank data or traffic figures that would separate "unseen" from "seen and not chosen."

## What could this reading not show?

The two free agents that carried the old series — Free Clip Map (2,480 sold on 2026-11-07) and Hook Grader (77 sold) — do not appear in this extraction at all. The page now holds far more listings than the 30 shown in the extracted view, and the free agents sit beyond it. So the honest statement is narrow: **the free total of 2,557 from 2026-11-07 cannot be updated from this reading.** We do not report it as flat, and we do not report it as grown. It is unmeasured this time, and the next reading needs a view that reaches the older listings before any free-side number is claimed again.

The same limits as always apply to the paid side. The page shows sold counts and prices. It does not show collected payments, renewals, cancellations or refunds, so no revenue figure is claimed from these counts — a sold count of 4 on a monthly plan is not four months of revenue, and it is not proof that any subscription is still active today.

## How should a sold count on a marketplace page be read?

From eleven days of distance, three rules hold up:

1. **Compare counts only within the same view.** The 2026-11-07 extraction showed 30 agents including the free pair; the 2026-11-18 extraction shows a different 30. Totals built from different windows are not a trend line.
2. **Price-model changes are part of the reading.** Two of our three paid agents moved from weekly to monthly pricing between readings. A count that holds steady across a pricing change — Storytime at 3 — says something different from the same count under an unchanged price.
3. **A gap in readings is itself a finding.** This series used to be read daily. An 11-day gap means the Series Planner's move from 3 to 4 cannot be dated, and any jump or stall inside the gap is invisible. The count is a snapshot, not a story.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can the agents themselves be seen?

All of them are listed on our publisher page, [capafy.ai/publisher/Anicca](https://capafy.ai/publisher/Anicca). The TikTok script agents — the Series Continuity Planner and the Storytime Script — are the paid listings with movement so far.

### Does a sold count mean revenue?

No. It means the marketplace displays that many sales against the listing. Payments collected, renewals and refunds are not shown on the public page, so this article claims counts and displayed prices only.

### Why did the free total disappear from this series?

It did not disappear from the page; it disappeared from the extracted view, because the listing order puts newer agents first and the view is limited to 30. Until a reading covers the older listings again, the free side is reported as unmeasured rather than guessed.

### Where are the earlier readings?

The previous reading, from 2026-11-07, is [Morning re-read: free climbs to 2,557, paid moves to 8](https://aniccaai.com/blog/capafy-free-agents-update-2026-11-04), and the full set sits in the [Capafy Agents category hub](https://aniccaai.com/blog/c/ai-creator-tools). For the hook-writing side of the same work, see [Hooks that get views](https://aniccaai.com/blog/hooks-that-get-views). The agents are one surface of what we build; the product at the centre is the [Anicca app](https://aniccaai.com/affirmation-app).

*Measurement note: all counts and prices above were read from the public Capafy publisher page for Anicca on 2026-11-18 (extracted view of 30 agents). The comparison reading is the same page on the morning of 2026-11-07, recorded in the article linked above. Sold counts are the marketplace's displayed figures, not payment records.*
